text:
Marta: Heads-up — nightly maintenance window this Wed 02:00 UTC will evict preemptible GPUs in us-west-2 for ~45m. Need a quick throughput impact estimate before we approve extension. Q: will concurrent request queues overflow and push p99 token latency >1s?

Raj: If we evict ~30% of preemptible slab, our sim shows tokens/sec drops ~22% and concurrent queue length up 1.8x on the shoulder. p95 from ~280ms -> ~450ms; p99 jumps a lot.

Lee: Quick extract I ran against perf DB (7d shoulder window):
```sql
SELECT region, SUM(gpu_hours) AS gpu_hours, AVG(tokens_per_sec) AS avg_tps
FROM perf_samples
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '7 days' AND window = 'shoulder'
GROUP BY region;
```

Lee: us-west-2 preemptible gpu_hours = 4300, avg_tps = 11200 tokens/sec. That's with preemptible share ~40%.

Ana: Eviction rate for preemptibles last week during comparable windows: baseline 6%/hr, spikes to ~18% when provider maintenance aligns. So risk is non-trivial.

Chris: Ops summary: scheduled down gpus = 16. Warm pool currently = 8 GPUs. We can bump warm pool to 24 for the window but cost estimate is ~+$2.5k/mo (pro-rated for extra reserved hours). Tradeoffs? :money_with_wings:

Kai: Minimal sim I ran (simplified):
```text
scenario: evict 16/48 gpus in us-west-2
concurrency: +40%
tokens/sec: -18%
queue_depth: 1.9x
p99_latency: 1.4s
headroom_remaining: ~12%
```

Raj: That ~12% headroom is optimistic — depends on model mix. If traffic tilts toward chat/generation-heavy models, headroom drops to ~4% and p99 exceeds 1.2s.

Marta: Options on the table: a) stagger maintenance per AZ to avoid simultaneous evictions, b) expand warm pool for the 2h around window, c) route ~15% traffic to eu-west-1 during the window (higher TTFB but protects p99). Which one is fastest to implement?

Lee: Staggering AZ-by-AZ seems lowest risk. Ops change: maintenance controller needs to support 10m offsets per AZ. I can patch the controller and run smoke tests.

Ana: Also propose autoscaler override: cap preemptible eviction to 8%/hr during our maintenance window so we don't get mass churn. Feels like a safe guard.

Chris: Cost note: routing 15% traffic to eu-west-1 increases egress and reserved usage, roughly +$800/day for the window if sustained, but it eliminates the p99 spike risk. We should only do it if dry-run shows significant tail risks.

Kai: Suggestion: run a dry-run next Tue 02:00 UTC with synthetic load that mirrors shoulder mix, measure queueing and p99, iterate. I can schedule the synthetic generator.

ops-bot: @channel Maintenance scheduled: us-west-2 patch window Wed 02:00 UTC -> 02:45 UTC. Please ack if you want to modify.

Marta: Ack. I'll open a short RFC with recommended AZ-stagger + dry-run and tag infra. cc @oncall
